title: Integrality over affine groupoid invariants
statement: Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$ and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ [def-pc-fibre-product] are morphisms such that, functorially in every test scheme $H$, $U(H)$ is the object set and $R(H)$ the arrow set of a groupoid with source $s$, target $t$, identity $e$, inverse $i$ and composition $c$. Write $\sigma=s^\sharp,\tau=t^\sharp:A\to B$ and $C=\{a\in A:\sigma(a)=\tau(a)\}$. Assume $s,t$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Then $A$ is integral over $C$: every $a\in A$ satisfies a monic polynomial in $C[T]$.

proof.text: If $U$ is empty then $A$ is the zero ring and its unique element is annihilated by $T\in C[T]$. Otherwise apply [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-invariant-rank-strata]. It gives a nonempty finite set $I$ of positive ranks and affine invariant pieces $U_r,R_r$ with both restricted projections of degree $r$. Put $A_r=\Gamma(U_r,\mathcal O)$ and $B_r=\Gamma(R_r,\mathcal O)$, and write $\sigma_r,\tau_r:A_r\to B_r$ for their source and target maps. The restricted identity is still a section of both projections. We will construct a monic annihilator separately on each such piece, then combine them.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-disjoint-union-product] repeatedly to the structure sheaves and these finite disjoint open decompositions. Restriction gives $A\cong\prod_{r\in I}A_r$ and $B\cong\prod_{r\in I}B_r$. Because $s^{-1}(U_r)=t^{-1}(U_r)=R_r$, the maps $\sigma,\tau$ have components $\sigma_r,\tau_r$ under these identifications. Thus an element $(a_r)_r$ is in $C$ exactly when $\sigma_r(a_r)=\tau_r(a_r)$ for every $r$. Hence $C\cong\prod_{r\in I}C_r$, where $C_r=\{a_r\in A_r:\sigma_r(a_r)=\tau_r(a_r)\}$. This last assertion is just equality in a product, not a claim that invariants commute with an arbitrary base change.

source.place: Tag 03BJ (groupoids-lemma-integral-over-invariants), proof, first paragraph: componentwise reduction

proof.text: Fix $a\in A$, and let $a_r$ be its component on $U_r$. Apply [lem-a1-finite-locally-free-norm-characteristic-polynomial] to $\varphi=\sigma_r$ and $b=\tau_r(a_r)$. Its hypothesis is precisely the degree-$r$ finite local freeness of $s_r$. It gives $P_r(T)=N_{\sigma_r[T]}(T-\tau_r(a_r))\in A_r[T]$, of the form $T^r+\sum_{j<r}p_{r,j}T^j$, and the equality $\bigl(\sigma_r[T](P_r)\bigr)(\tau_r(a_r))=0$ in $B_r$. This does not assume $B_r$ is globally free over $A_r$.

source.place: Tag 03BJ (groupoids-lemma-integral-over-invariants), proof, second paragraph: norm polynomial and Cayley-Hamilton

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-polynomial-norm-invariant] to the restricted groupoid $(U_r,R_r)$ and $F=T-a_r\in A_r[T]$. Since $\tau_r[T]$ fixes $T$, its norm $Q_F$ is exactly the $P_r$ just constructed. That lemma gives $P_r\in C_r[T]$. Explicitly, for every coefficient $p_{r,j}$ we have $\sigma_r(p_{r,j})=\tau_r(p_{r,j})$. This supplies invariant coefficients rather than assuming that the norm itself descends without a theorem.

source.place: Tag 03BJ (groupoids-lemma-integral-over-invariants), proof, second paragraph: determinant trick after adjoining x

proof.text: The equality of the two images of each coefficient gives $\bigl(\sigma_r[T](P_r)\bigr)(\tau_r(a_r))=\sum_j\tau_r(p_{r,j})\tau_r(a_r)^j=\tau_r(P_r(a_r))$. Step 3 therefore gives $\tau_r(P_r(a_r))=0$. The ring map $e_r^\sharp:B_r\to A_r$ satisfies $e_r^\sharp\circ\tau_r=\operatorname{id}_{A_r}$ because $t_r\circ e_r=\operatorname{id}_{U_r}$. Apply it to obtain $P_r(a_r)=0$. This is the explicit injectivity needed for the final descent of the annihilation equation.

source.place: Tag 03BJ (groupoids-lemma-integral-over-invariants), proof, final sentences; the identity section supplies the injectivity there obtained from faithful flatness

proof.text: Let $d=\max I$. For each $r\in I$, set $Q_r(T)=T^{d-r}P_r(T)\in C_r[T]$. Every $Q_r$ has the form $T^d+\sum_{j<d}q_{r,j}T^j$ and vanishes at $a_r$. For each $j<d$, the finite tuple $(q_{r,j})_r$ is a single coefficient $q_j\in C$ by step 2. Then $Q(T)=T^d+\sum_{j<d}q_jT^j\in C[T]$ is monic, and the components of $Q(a)$ in $A\cong\prod_rA_r$ are exactly $Q_r(a_r)=0$. Hence $Q(a)=0$. Since $a$ was arbitrary, $A$ is integral over $C$.
